reversals.english: internal emptiness is established to reverse the apprehension of external things as the consumed
reversals.why: source and reference present OUTER emptiness here; T1 names its opposite, internal emptiness

items.source: དེ་ལྟར་ནང་གི་དངོས་པོ་ལ་ཟ་བ་པོར་འཛིན་པ་བཟློག་ནས་ཕྱི་རོལ་གྱི་དངོས་པོ་ལ་བཟའ་བར་འཛིན་པ་བཟློག་པའི་ཕྱིར་ཕྱི་སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་རྣམ་པར་གཞག་སྟེ།
items.english: Having thus reversed the apprehension of internal things as a consumer , internal emptiness is established to reverse the apprehension of external things as the consumed .
items.why: The source says internal emptiness is established to reverse the apprehension of internal things, and external emptiness is established to reverse the apprehension of external things. The English incorrectly links the reversal of the consumer to the establishment of internal emptiness, and the reversal of the consumed to the establishment of external emptiness in a way that misrepresents the causal structure of the text.

items.b: ནང་སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་དུ་བཞག་གོ །
items.why: A identifies the following section as 'outer emptiness' (phyi stong pa nyid), while B identifies it as 'inner emptiness' (nang stong pa nyid).

defects: T8: Huang: 無所不為 (nothing one does not do) rendered 'one does nothing'

items.source: 為道者已聞道者也已聞道而為之不得不無為而已
items.english: One who practices the Way has already heard the Way. Having heard the Way, one has to do nothing but non-action.
items.why: The English translates '為道者' (one who practices the Way) as 'One who practices the Way', but the source text defines '為道' as the act of practicing the Way, not the person.

items.a: 未聞道而求之不得不博故曰益
items.b: 未聞道，故必廣學以求之，故曰損之又損。
items.why: A identifies 'increasing' (益) with the pursuit of learning before knowing the Way; B identifies this same pursuit as 'decreasing' (損之又損).

items.a: 已聞道而為之不得不無為而已故曰損
items.b: 行道者，已聞道矣。既聞道，則無事乎無為，故曰損。
items.why: A says one who knows the Way must practice 'non-action' (無為) and calls this 'decreasing' (損); B says one who knows the Way has no need for 'non-action' and calls this 'decreasing' (損).

items.source: prius igitur occurrit intellectui nostro cognoscere animal et cognoscere homine.
items.english: Therefore, it occurs to our intellect first to know "animal" and to know "man."

items.source: et quod cognitio singularium est prior quo ad nos et cognitio uniuersalis cognitio sensitiua et cognitio intellectiua. si et sensum et cum intellectu cognitio magis et est prior et cognitio minoris et cois.
items.english: And that the cognition of singulars is prior as to us, and the cognition of universal [is posterior]. Sensitive cognition and intellectual cognition, if it is sense and with intellect, the cognition [of the more] is prior and the cognition of the less and common [is posterior].
items.why: The English text contradicts itself within the same sentence regarding whether the more universal or the less universal is prior.

items.source: et hoc modo magis et est pus et in nam quod apparet manifeste in generatione bo minis et aialis. naz prius generatur animal bo: ut et or in in libro de generatione animalium.
items.english: And in this mode, the more [universal] is prior in nature, which appears manifestly in the generation of man and animal. For the animal is generated before the man, as Aristotle says in the book On the Generation of Animals .
items.why: The source says animal is generated before man; the English swaps the order in the first clause, claiming man is generated before animal.

items.source: sic igitur animal consideratum in se pus et in nostra cognitione et bo. si bo et pus i nra cognitione et animal sic per ronis eius.
items.english: Thus, therefore, animal considered in itself is prior in our cognition, and man [is posterior]. If man [is prior] in our cognition, then animal [is posterior] by its reason.
items.why: The English text asserts that animal is prior in cognition, then immediately asserts the opposite (if man is prior, animal is posterior).

items.source: شه چو سرهنگش این حکایت گفت
items.english: When the King heard this tale from his colonel
items.why: The source says the King told the tale to his colonel (sarehang), not that he heard it from him.

items.b: به یک دست آن شصت‌نردبان بَرَد | چنان کز نشستن نماند خرد

items.b: اگر کس دمی برکشد از غلوم
items.why: A refers to breathing/living; B uses 'gholum' (likely a corruption or different term) changing the context of the challenge.

items.b: zonder middeling met God in deze eenheid
items.why: A claims there is a medium/means, B claims there is no medium (zonder middeling).

items.b: de vruchtgevende neiging van de geest
items.why: A refers to 'customary/habitual' (ghebruyckelijcke), B refers to 'fruit-bearing' (vruchtgevende).

items.b: བསོད་ནམས་ཆེན་པོ་ཞེས་པ་ནི་སྐྱེས་བུ་ཆེན་པོ་ལ་བྱའོ།
items.why: A defines 'skal chen' as 'great self', while B defines 'bsod nams chen po' as 'great person'.

items.b: དམ་ཚིག་ནི་སྙོམས་པར་འཇུག་པ་ལ་སོགས་པ་ལ་བྱའོ།
items.why: A identifies the term as 'vow' (sdom pa), while B identifies it as 'samaya' (dam tshig).

items.b: དབུ་མ་ནི་ལམ་སྟེ་དོན་ནི་སེམས་གཉིས་ཀྱི་རང་བཞིན་གྱིས་མེད་པ་དང་གཉིས་ཀ་སྟོང་པའི་རང་བཞིན་གྱིས་མེད་པ་མ་ཡིན་པའོ།
items.why: B negates the existence of the two-fold nature, whereas A negates the existence of the two-fold nature but affirms the emptiness.

items.source: 勝者乃揖不勝者升取
items.english: The winner then bows, and the one who is not the winner ascends to take the cup and drink.
items.why: The source says the winner bows and the loser ascends to take the cup; the English implies the winner bows while the loser ascends, but the source text does not specify the winner bows while the loser ascends to drink as a sequence of two separate actions, but rather describes the ritual procedure of the loser taking the cup.

items.b: 勝者揖，不勝者升取觶而飲
items.why: A implies the winner bows (and the loser drinks), while B explicitly states the winner bows and the loser drinks.

reversals.english: The phlemys (a type of fish) is particularly clever, guileless, and prudent

defects: T9: begins at 'For they are full of many devices' (ἐπεὶ μάλα πολλὰ ... μηχανόωνται); the Hermes invocation and ~17 lines on the fisher's body, leaping and diving are absent
T7: 'The phlemys ... a type of fish' for garbled 'φλημής δὲ μάλιστα, καὶ ἄβομος ἠδὲ σαόφρων' — reference: the fisher should be daring, dauntless, temperate
T10: gloss 'likely a species of bass or similar' invents a fish; the lines describe the fisherman
mistranslation: 'It endures winter twice over' for 'φέροι καὶ χεῖμα ... καὶ ῥίγιον ὥρη σερίκ' (winter and the season of Sirius)
mistranslation: 'In winter ... it is captured ... by manifold nets, it is raised' for 'σέλλεσθαι ... αἴραις παντόμοισιν ὀφίλλεται' (set out with the sun; spring day prospers every kind of fishing)
T9: first 18 verses absent: invocation 'ἑρμεία κλυτόβυλε', and the fisher's body 'πραιπνὰ, καὶ ἄλκιμα' through 'ψυχὴν δ’ ... νοήμων'; candidate opens at 'For they are full of many devices'

items.source: φλημής δὲ μάλιστα, καὶ ἄβομος ἠδὲ σαόφρων ζῇ.
items.english: The phlemys is particularly clever, guileless, and prudent.
items.why: The Greek word 'ἄβομος' (or 'ἄδολος') is translated as 'guileless', but in this context, it contradicts the preceding description of the fish as 'πολυπαίπαλος' (very crafty/deceitful).

items.a: φλημής δὲ μάλιστα, καὶ ἄβομος ἠδὲ σαόφρων ζῇ.
items.b: φλεμὺς δὲ μάλιστα σοφός τε καὶ ἀδόλιος καὶ περίφρων.
items.why: A describes the fish as 'abomos' (un-altared/simple/foolish), while B describes it as 'adolos' (guileless/cunning-free) and 'periphron' (very wise).

items.a: χείματι δ’ ἠελίοιο βολαῖς ἅμα κιδναμένησε σέλλεσθαι
items.b: ἐν δὲ χειμῶνι, ἅμα ἀκτῖσιν ἡλίου σκεδαννύμενος, ἁλίσκεται
items.why: A says the fish is scattered/dispersed by sunbeams in winter; B says the fish is caught (halisketai) by them.

items.b: རྡོ་རྗེ་སེམས་དཔའ་ཞེས་པ་ནི་སེམས་བརྟན་པའོ། དེས་ང་རྒྱལ་བྱའོ།
items.why: A interprets 'b-snyems-pa' as 'pride/arrogance' (or being proud), while B interprets it as 'pride' (nga-rgyal) as a separate instruction.

items.b: རྐང་པ་ནི་ལོང་བུའོ།

the Roman people, who were rightly governed

defects: mistranslation: 'seed of civil wars ever arisen from any other cause than when' for 'semen a causa [de]erit, du[m]' (will never be wanting while)
T7: 'flourished with the spear ... until the thirty-sixth year' garbles 'cu vibrass ... sexto trigesimo anno post a sceleratioze hasta'
T8: 'metui quam' (feared rather than) lost; says 'preferred to be loved'
T8: 'we preferred to be loved when we wished to be dear' inverts 'metui quam cari'
T7: 'only by the piety of others' from OCR 'pietes' (parietes, walls)

items.source: Iure igitur plectim.
items.english: Rightly, therefore, are we punished.
items.why: The Latin 'plectim' (plectimur) is passive, but the context of the argument implies the subject is the Roman people/state being punished by the gods/fate, whereas the English 'we' implies the speaker and audience are the agents of their own punishment.

items.source: du hoies pdia hasta illa crues ta et meminerme t sperabur.
items.english: when men have remembered those bloody spears and hoped for them.
items.why: The Latin 'sperabur' (sperabantur) is passive ('were hoped for'), but the English translates it as active ('hoped for them').

items.source: du mes tui. q. cari esset diligi maluimus.
items.english: if we preferred to be loved when we wished to be dear.
items.why: The Latin 'cari esset' (cari esse) means 'to be dear', but the English reverses the logic of the comparison between being loved and being dear.
